description_good_justification: README.md opening line and GitHub repo description both state the purpose succinctly: 'C2PA manifest discovery over HTTP: the c2pa-manifest Link header (RFC 8288), with a Tower middleware' (README.md:1-3; `gh repo view` description field).
interact_justification: README.md documents install (crates.io/npm/PyPI, README.md:23-33), links to SECURITY.md for vulnerability reports (README.md:204-206), and CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to fork/PR (CONTRIBUTING.md:9-33). GitHub Issues is enabled (`gh repo view` hasIssuesEnabled: true).
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md:9-33 documents the process: fork, branch from main, add tests, run cargo test/clippy/fmt, open a PR.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md:27-37 specifies acceptance requirements: cargo test --all-features, cargo clippy --all-features -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all -- --check, and Conventional Commits style.
floss_license_justification: Cargo.toml:8 declares `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`, both OSI-approved FLOSS licenses.
floss_license_osi_justification: Both licenses used (MIT, LICENSE-MIT; Apache-2.0, LICENSE-APACHE) are OSI-approved licenses.
license_location_justification: LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT hold the full texts (dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 per Cargo.toml); a top-level LICENSE file (identical to LICENSE-APACHE) is also present at the repository root for tooling that only recognizes that exact filename.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md provides overview, usage examples (Serve it / Read it sections), feature table, and install instructions. src/lib.rs:5-40 has crate-level rustdoc.
documentation_interface_justification: Public API is documented via rustdoc comments in src/lib.rs, src/link.rs, src/layer.rs, src/error.rs, published at docs.rs (badge in README.md:7), plus worked examples of header input/output format in README.md:78-149.
sites_https_justification: Repo (https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-http), crates.io, docs.rs, npm, and PyPI are all HTTPS-only sites; no plain-http URLs found in README.md or Cargo.toml.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled for this repo (`gh repo view` hasIssuesEnabled: true) and is URL-addressable (https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-http/issues), searchable, and open to any GitHub user without a proprietary client.
english_justification: All documentation (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, rustdoc comments) is written in English.
maintained_justification: git log shows active commits through 2026-08-22 (`git log -1 --format=%cd` => Sat Aug 22 18:11:13 2026), with 16+ commits since project start on 2026-07-31, including dependency bumps and security hardening (c25bb4f, 0077fff).
repo_public_justification: Repo is public at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-http (`gh repo view` isPrivate: false).
repo_track_justification: Git history records author, timestamp, and change for every commit (`git log --format='%ci %an'`); e.g. '047e7da docs: add title and tagline...' by David Condrey.
repo_interim_justification: git log shows 16+ commits between the only tagged release (v0.1.0) and the current Cargo.toml version 0.2.0, including intermediate fixes and features (5d77f70, 6a0947f, e5102db).
repo_distributed_justification: Project uses git, a distributed VCS, hosted on GitHub.
version_unique_justification: Cargo.toml:3 carries a unique `version` field per release; the release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml) enforces the git tag matches this version before publishing.
version_semver_justification: Cargo.toml:3 uses SemVer (currently 0.2.0); release.yml tags follow `v*.*.*`.
version_tags_justification: git tag -l shows `v0.1.0`; release.yml is triggered by pushing a `v*.*.*` tag.
release_notes_justification: The only release (v0.1.0) was created via `gh release create --title "$tag" --generate-notes` (.github/workflows/release.yml:187-193), which is GitHub's auto-generated PR-list notes rather than curated, human-written release notes. cliff.toml configures git-cliff for Keep-a-Changelog-style notes, but no CHANGELOG.md exists in the repo and git-cliff is not wired into the release workflow yet.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed in any release to date (single release v0.1.0, no CVEs or security advisories on the repo).
report_process_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled with structured templates at .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml and feature_request.yml; CONTRIBUTING.md:11-14 documents the reporting process.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is used as the tracker (`gh repo view` hasIssuesEnabled: true), with dedicated bug_report.yml and feature_request.yml templates.
report_responses_justification: No qualifying reports exist to assess a majority against (evidence: The repo currently has zero open issues (`gh repo view` issues.totalCount: 0), so there are no unacknowledged bug reports in the last 2-12 months; the process is in place and untested by volume.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met — flag for maintainer confirmation if/when real reports arrive.
enhancement_responses_justification: No qualifying enhancement requests exist to assess a majority against (evidence: No enhancement requests have been filed to date (0 open issues per `gh repo view`); a feature_request.yml template exists to receive them.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues provides a public, searchable, permanent archive of reports and responses at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-http/issues.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents the process: private GitHub Security Advisory or email admin@writerslogic.com, and explicitly says not to use public issues (SECURITY.md:7-13). Note the advisory link in SECURITY.md:12 points to `c2pa-zip/security/advisories/new` (a sibling crate's repo) rather than `c2pa-http` -- a copy/paste artifact that should be fixed, though the email channel and the general process are still valid.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md:11-13 gives a private-report path (GitHub Security Advisories, or email admin@writerslogic.com).
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received in the last 6 months (no security advisories on the repo, no history of any); SECURITY.md states an initial response is expected within a few days.
build_justification: Cargo is the build system (Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock); CI runs `cargo check`, `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` in .github/workflows/ci.yml:37-42.
build_common_tools_justification: Uses Cargo, the standard Rust build tool, plus wasm-pack and maturin for the npm/PyPI targets (.github/workflows/release.yml), all standard tools for their respective language ecosystems.
build_floss_tools_justification: Cargo, rustc, wasm-pack, and maturin/PyO3 are all FLOSS; no proprietary build tools are used anywhere in Cargo.toml or .github/workflows/*.yml.
test_justification: Automated FLOSS test suite exists: unit tests in src/link.rs (28 #[test] fns) and src/layer.rs (7), plus tests/link_header.rs (12 integration tests). CONTRIBUTING.md:24 documents `cargo test` to run it.
test_invocation_justification: `cargo test` is the standard Rust invocation, documented in CONTRIBUTING.md:24 and run in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml 'test' job, and release.yml:52).
test_most_justification: 47 total test functions (28 in src/link.rs, 7 in src/layer.rs, 12 in tests/link_header.rs) cover header parsing edge cases: quoted/unquoted rel, multiple Link fields, embedded-manifest childlabel stripping, CRLF/injection encoding, and the Tower layer behavior.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs a 'test' job (cargo test) and a 'msrv' job on every push/PR to main.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md:30 explicitly requires 'Make changes, add tests, run cargo test --all-features' as part of Submitting Changes.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent feature commits pair code with tests, e.g. '5d77f70 feat: uniform Error::code, verified MSRV, and integration tests' and 'e5102db feat: C2PA manifest discovery via the c2pa-manifest Link header' which introduced tests/link_header.rs alongside src/link.rs.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md:30 documents the test-addition policy directly in the contribution instructions.
warnings_justification: CI runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy --features python -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:39-41).
warnings_fixed_justification: Clippy/fmt run with `-D warnings` in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:39-41) and release.yml, which fails the build on any warning, so warnings cannot merge unaddressed.
warnings_strict_justification: No `[lints]` table in Cargo.toml and no `#![warn(clippy::pedantic)]`/`clippy::nursery` attributes in src/lib.rs; only default clippy lints are enabled with `-D warnings`, not the maximally strict lint groups.
know_secure_design_justification: README.md 'Header injection is impossible, without rejecting anything' (README.md:121-148) and 'Scope' (README.md:150-157) sections show deliberate secure-design reasoning: percent-encoding to prevent CRLF header injection, and explicitly refusing to buffer response bodies to avoid an unbounded-memory DoS. src/lib.rs:70 sets `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.
know_common_errors_justification: Same evidence as know_secure_design: README.md documents mitigation of HTTP response-splitting/header-injection (CRLF encoding) and denial-of-service via unbounded body buffering (README.md:121-157), both common vulnerability classes for HTTP-adjacent code.
crypto_published_justification: This crate parses/serialises an HTTP Link header only; it performs no cryptographic operations (confirmed by reading src/link.rs, src/layer.rs, src/error.rs; no crypto crates in Cargo.toml dependencies).
crypto_call_justification: No cryptographic functionality is implemented or called anywhere in this crate.
crypto_keylength_justification: No cryptographic keys are used or generated by this crate.
crypto_working_justification: No cryptographic algorithms are used by this crate.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No cryptographic algorithms are used by this crate.
crypto_pfs_justification: This crate performs no network key agreement; it only formats/parses an HTTP header string.
crypto_password_storage_justification: This crate stores no passwords or credentials of any kind.
crypto_random_justification: No cryptographic keys or nonces are generated by this crate.
delivery_mitm_justification: Packages are delivered via crates.io, npm, and PyPI, all served exclusively over HTTPS, and installed with `cargo add`/`npm install`/`pip install` which use HTTPS registries (README.md:23-33).
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash-only integrity check is fetched over plain HTTP; all package registries (crates.io, npm, PyPI) are HTTPS-only and perform their own registry-level integrity verification.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No publicly known medium-or-higher vulnerabilities are open against this repo (no security advisories exist); one dependency security fix (pyo3 bump, commit 0077fff 'fix(security): bump pyo3 to 0.29') was applied promptly.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerabilities have been reported against this project; when a dependency security issue was identified it was fixed promptly (commit 0077fff 'fix(security): bump pyo3 to 0.29').
no_leaked_credentials_justification: `grep -rn` for secret/api_key/password/token patterns across the repo found only legitimate CI secret *references* (CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN via `${{ secrets.* }}`/`${{ github.token }}`), no literal credential values.
static_analysis_justification: Clippy (a FLOSS static analysis tool for Rust) runs on every push/PR and before every release (.github/workflows/ci.yml:39-40, release.yml:51-52).
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: Only default clippy lints are enabled (`cargo clippy -- -D warnings`); no dedicated vulnerability-focused scanner (e.g. cargo-audit, cargo-deny, CodeQL, semgrep) is configured. scorecard.yml only runs OpenSSF Scorecard, whose SARIF upload is a supply-chain score, not a source vulnerability scan.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CI fails the build on any clippy warning (`-D warnings`, .github/workflows/ci.yml:39-40), so medium+ static-analysis findings cannot be merged unaddressed.
static_analysis_often_justification: Clippy runs on every push to main and every pull request (.github/workflows/ci.yml `on: push/pull_request`).
dynamic_analysis_justification: A cargo-fuzz target (fuzz/fuzz_targets/parse_untrusted.rs) drives the crate's untrusted-input parsers with libFuzzer; fuzz/README.md documents how to run it.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The crate forbids unsafe code entirely (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, src/lib.rs:70), so there is no memory-unsafe code requiring a memory-safety dynamic analysis tool.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The fuzz target builds with cargo-fuzz's default dev profile, which enables debug assertions and overflow checks, so Rust's integer-overflow and bounds checks act as assertions during fuzzing.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is in use, so there are no dynamic-analysis findings to fix.
